title: CM Solar Pump Yojana MP: Subsidy, Registration, Eligibility
meta_description: CM Solar Pump Yojana MP gives farmers up to 90% subsidy on solar irrigation pumps. Register at cmsolarpump.mp.gov.in. Check eligibility and application steps.

hero.one_liner: Madhya Pradesh gives farmers up to 90% subsidy on solar irrigation pumps under Kusum B. Subsidy share, farmer cost, registration, and how to apply.

what_is_it: Mukhyamantri Solar Pump Yojana (also called Kusum B in MP) is a Madhya Pradesh government scheme that subsidises solar irrigation pumps for farmers. The central and state governments together provide up to 90% of the pump cost, and the farmer pays only the remaining share plus a registration fee of Rs 5,000 at the time of application.

Mukhyamantri Solar Pump Yojana is officially categorised under the Kusum B component of the central PM Kusum scheme, which means funding comes from both the central government and the Madhya Pradesh state government. The combined subsidy can reach up to approximately 90% of the total pump cost for eligible farmers.

The scheme was launched on 17 February 2020 by the New and Renewable Energy Department of MP. It is implemented on the ground by Madhya Pradesh Urja Vikas Nigam Limited (MPUVNL), which manages applications, vendor selection, and installation coordination.

how_to_apply.title: Check eligibility before applying
how_to_apply.description: Confirm that you are a permanent resident of Madhya Pradesh with agricultural land and a Kisan Card. Your land must currently have no active permanent electricity connection, or you must be willing to surrender the electricity connection for that khasra (plot) before the solar pump is installed.

how_to_apply.title: Gather all required documents
how_to_apply.description: Collect your Samagra ID, bank account details linked to Aadhaar, caste declaration, khasra (land record) for the irrigation site, and the technical specifications of the solar pump size you need. The khasra number is required to verify that no permanent electricity connection exists on that land parcel.

how_to_apply.title: Apply online at cmsolarpump.mp.gov.in
how_to_apply.description: Visit the official portal at cmsolarpump.mp.gov.in and fill the online application form with your personal details, Samagra ID, land details, and preferred pump capacity. Submit the application along with the Rs 5,000 registration fee paid online to Madhya Pradesh Urja Vikas Nigam Limited.

how_to_apply.title: Wait for selection and demand note
how_to_apply.description: Applications are processed in priority order based on budget availability. When your application is selected, MPUVNL will issue a demand note specifying the balance amount (the farmer's share of the pump cost after deducting the subsidy). You must pay this balance within 20 days of receiving the demand note.

how_to_apply.title: Make the balance payment
how_to_apply.description: Pay the balance amount to Madhya Pradesh Urja Vikas Nigam CM Solar Pump Scheme through NEFT, RTGS, cheque, or demand draft within the 20-day window. Failure to pay within this period may result in your slot being passed to the next applicant in the queue.

how_to_apply.title: Solar pump installation at your site
how_to_apply.description: After receiving your full payment, MPUVNL arranges for a registered vendor to install the solar pump at your field. Installation is completed within approximately 90 days of your payment, after which the complete solar pumping system is handed over to you for use.

extra_sections.title: Government Subsidy on the Pump
extra_sections.desc:
The headline subsidy is up to about 90%, funded jointly by the centre and MP state.

In practice the exact share varies by pump type, so a 5 HP system can still mean a farmer contribution of around Rs 72,000. Always check your demand note for the precise amount.

extra_sections.heading: How the Subsidy and Eligibility Work

items.title: Kusum B funding
items.sub: Officially under the Kusum B component of central PM Kusum, so funding comes from both the centre and MP state, reaching up to ~90%.

items.title: Target farmer
items.sub: A farmer with no permanent electricity connection for irrigation on the relevant khasra, who otherwise relies on costly diesel or seasonal water.

items.title: Surrender condition
items.sub: Farmers with an existing connection can apply but must surrender it before installation. The government does not give dual support for one plot.

items.title: Pump range
items.sub: Capacity runs 1 HP to 7.5 HP. For 5 HP and below, only DC pumps are installed and AC applications are auto-converted to DC.

extra_sections.text: A solar pump under this scheme replaces years of diesel and electricity costs with a one-time subsidised investment. After the government covers up to 90% of the pump price, the farmer's remaining share is a small fraction of what the same capacity diesel pump would cost to run in a single season.

extra_sections.heading: Documents Required for CM Solar Pump Yojana

items.title: Samagra ID
items.sub: Your Samagra family ID, used to pull verified family and residence details into the application.

items.title: Aadhaar-linked bank account
items.sub: Bank account details linked to Aadhaar, since the subsidy and any refund move through DBT.

items.title: Khasra (land record)
items.sub: The land record for the irrigation site, used to confirm no permanent electricity connection exists on that plot.

items.title: Caste declaration
items.sub: A caste declaration as required by the application form.

items.title: Pump specification
items.sub: The technical specification of the pump capacity you need, from 1 HP up to 7.5 HP.

extra_sections.title: The Electricity Connection Condition
extra_sections.content:
Priority goes to farmers in areas where power companies have not set up grid infrastructure, so the plot has no permanent electricity connection for irrigation.

If you already have a permanent connection on that khasra, you must agree to surrender it before installation. The government does not give dual support, both grid electricity and a subsidised solar pump, for the same plot.

extra_sections.heading: After the Solar Pump Is Installed

items.title: No electricity or diesel bills
items.sub: The pump runs on sunlight, so there are no monthly electricity charges and no diesel cost for irrigation.

items.title: Long working life
items.sub: Solar pumps typically last 20 to 25 years with minimal upkeep, making the one-time subsidised cost a long-term investment.

items.title: Sell surplus power
items.sub: Where net metering applies, surplus electricity can be sold to the local DISCOM, creating a small extra income stream. This varies by local policy.

items.title: Basic maintenance
items.sub: Clean the panels every few weeks so dust does not cut output, and check electrical connections periodically. Contact the vendor for any technical issue.

extra_sections.title: If Your Site Is Found Unsuitable
extra_sections.content:
If the solar pump site is found unsuitable or not selected after inspection, MPUVNL refunds the Rs 5,000 registration amount.

No interest is paid on this refund. For unresolved issues you can raise a grievance through MPUVNL or, if needed, file an RTI to get an official response on your application status.

extra_sections.title: Why MP Pushes Solar Pumps Over Diesel
extra_sections.content:
Farmers in areas with weak grid infrastructure run diesel pumps for irrigation, which are costly to fuel and polluting. A solar pump removes that recurring cost entirely.

The scheme targets exactly these off-grid plots first, where the government would otherwise have to set up temporary electricity connections. Replacing them with solar cuts both farmer cost and state power burden.

items.title: You pay only the balance
items.sub: The central and state subsidy is adjusted into the system cost up front. You pay only the remaining farmer share shown on your demand note, plus the Rs 5,000 registration fee.

items.title: DBT for refunds
items.sub: Any refund of the registration fee, if your site is unsuitable, is sent by Direct Benefit Transfer to your Aadhaar-linked bank account.

items.title: Priority by budget
items.sub: Applications are cleared in priority order against available budget. Off-grid plots without an existing connection are taken up first.

items.title: Pump tied to you
items.sub: The installed pump cannot be transferred or sold. It stays tied to the registered farmer and the specific land plot.

extra_sections.heading: The Three PM-Kusum Components, in Short

steps.title: Component A
steps.desc: Ground-mounted solar power plants set up by farmers or groups on barren or fallow land.

steps.title: Component B (this scheme)
steps.desc: Standalone solar agriculture pumps for off-grid farmers, which is what MP runs as CM Solar Pump Yojana.

steps.title: Component C
steps.desc: Solarisation of existing grid-connected pumps so farmers can use solar by day and sell surplus.

faqs.question: What is CM Solar Pump Yojana MP?
faqs.answer: CM Solar Pump Yojana (Kusum B) is a Madhya Pradesh government scheme that subsidises solar irrigation pumps for farmers. The central and state governments together provide up to approximately 90% of the pump cost, and the farmer pays the remaining share plus a Rs 5,000 registration fee.

faqs.question: How much subsidy does CM Solar Pump Yojana give?
faqs.answer: The scheme provides up to approximately 90% subsidy on the total cost of the solar pump, with contributions from both the central government and the Madhya Pradesh state government. The exact farmer contribution depends on the pump capacity selected and the current rate card published by MPUVNL.

faqs.question: How do I register for CM Solar Pump Yojana MP?
faqs.answer: Visit the official portal at cmsolarpump.mp.gov.in, fill the online application form with your Samagra ID, khasra details, and pump specifications, and pay the Rs 5,000 registration fee online to MPUVNL. Ensure you have a Kisan Card and that your land has no permanent electricity connection for irrigation.

faqs.question: What is the official portal for MP solar pump registration?
faqs.answer: The official portal is cmsolarpump.mp.gov.in. All applications, status tracking, and payment-related information for CM Solar Pump Yojana are managed through this portal by Madhya Pradesh Urja Vikas Nigam Limited.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for CM Solar Pump Yojana in MP?
faqs.answer: Farmers who are permanent residents of Madhya Pradesh, hold a Kisan Card, and have agricultural land without a permanent electricity connection for irrigation are eligible. Farmers with an existing electricity connection can also apply but must agree to surrender that connection after the solar pump is installed.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for CM Solar Pump Yojana application?
faqs.answer: You need your Samagra ID, Aadhaar-linked bank account details, caste declaration, khasra (land record) for the irrigation site, and the technical specifications of the solar pump capacity you are applying for. All documents must be submitted through the online portal at cmsolarpump.mp.gov.in.

faqs.question: How long does it take to install the solar pump after applying?
faqs.answer: After you pay the full balance amount (your share after subsidy), MPUVNL arranges installation within approximately 120 days. In special circumstances this timeline may be extended, but no additional cost is charged to the farmer.

faqs.question: Is the Rs 5,000 registration fee refundable?
faqs.answer:
Yes. The Rs 5,000 registration fee is fully refunded if the site is found unsuitable after inspection or if the applicant is not selected from the priority list.

The refund is made without interest.

faqs.question: Can I get a solar pump under cm solar pump mp gov if I already have an electricity connection?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you must surrender the permanent electricity connection on that khasra before the solar pump installation. The scheme does not allow dual support for the same irrigation plot, so the electricity connection must be disconnected as a condition of receiving the solar pump subsidy.

faqs.question: What pump sizes are available under CM Solar Pump Yojana?
faqs.answer:
The scheme covers solar pumps from 1 HP to 7.5 HP capacity. For pumps up to 5 HP, only DC (direct current) pumps are installed as per scheme rules.

Applications for 5 HP AC pumps are automatically converted to 5 HP DC pumps.
